class.name: SQLiteDatabase
class.brief_description: A connection to an SQLite database file.
class.description: [SQLiteDatabase] opens an SQLite 3 database file and runs SQL on it. All file access goes through [FileAccess], so databases work in [code]user://[/code] (also on the Web, where [code]user://[/code] is stored in IndexedDB), in absolute paths, and read-only in [code]res://[/code] and exported PCK files. [codeblock] var db = SQLiteDatabase.new() if db.open("user://save.db") != OK: push_error(db.get_last_error_message()) return db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (name TEXT, points INTEGER);") db.execute("INSERT INTO scores VALUES (?, ?);", ["Ada", 120]) for row in db.query("SELECT name, points FROM scores WHERE points > :min;", { "min": 100 }): print(row.name, ": ", row.points) db.close() [/codeblock] Parameters are passed as an [Array] for positional placeholders ([code]?[/code], [code]?1[/code]) or as a [Dictionary] for named placeholders ([code]:name[/code], [code]@name[/code], [code]$name[/code]; the keys are written without the prefix). Values map to SQLite types as follows: [code]null[/code] to NULL, [bool] and [int] to INTEGER, [float] to REAL, [String] and [StringName] to TEXT, [PackedByteArray] to BLOB. Other types are rejected with [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER]. Results come back as [int], [float], [String], [PackedByteArray] or [code]null[/code]. Methods return an [enum Error]; [method get_last_error_message] gives the details of the last failure. SQL errors are not printed to the output. The build includes FTS5 full-text search, the JSON functions and the math functions. Write-ahead logging (WAL) and loadable extensions are not available. Locks are not used: open each database file through one [SQLiteDatabase] at a time, and use one [SQLiteDatabase] from one thread at a time. [SQLiteDatabase] is a [Resource]: files ending in [code].db[/code], [code].sqlite[/code], [code].sqlite3[/code] or [code].db3[/code] can be loaded with [method @GDScript.load] or assigned to an exported property. Loading only creates the object; [method open] without a path then opens the loaded file. In the editor, selecting such a file shows its tables in the Inspector; the [b]Edit[/b] button next to a table opens a window to edit, insert and delete its rows. The files are exported as they are. Saving a new [SQLiteDatabase] with [method ResourceSaver.save] (or [b]Save[/b] in the editor) to one of these extensions creates an empty database file; an existing file is kept, and a database loaded from another file is copied. [codeblock] var db: SQLiteDatabase = load("res://data/items.db") db.open() # Read-only, like every file in res://. for table in db.get_table_names(): print(table, ": ", db.get_row_count(table), " rows") [/codeblock] The schema methods ([method get_table_names], [method has_table], [method get_columns], [method get_column_names], [method get_column_count], [method get_row_count]) take plain table names (no schema prefix) and never paste them into SQL unquoted. For an unknown table they return an empty result or [code]-1[/code] and set [method get_last_error] to [constant ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST]. [b]Note:[/b] [method @GDScript.load] returns the same object for the same file while it is in use. For a second, separate connection, create one with [code]SQLiteDatabase.new()[/code] and open the path explicitly. [b]Note:[/b] Databases in [code]res://[/code] are read-only for scripts, also in the editor (the editor's Database dock can still change them). To modify a database shipped with the project, copy it to [code]user://[/code] first, for example with [method DirAccess.copy_absolute]. [b]Note:[/b] On the Web, the rollback journal is kept in memory and the database file is written to IndexedDB on every commit.

method.name: begin_transaction
method.description: Starts a transaction ([code]BEGIN[/code]). Changes become permanent with [method commit] or are discarded with [method rollback]. Grouping many writes into one transaction is much faster than writing them one by one.

method.name: close
method.description: Closes the database and finalizes the [SQLiteStatement]s prepared from it: they stop working, and the file is no longer held open. Does nothing if the database is not open. The database is also closed when the [SQLiteDatabase] is freed.

method.name: commit
method.description: Commits the current transaction ([code]COMMIT[/code]). Returns [constant ERR_QUERY_FAILED] if no transaction is active.

method.name: execute
method.description: Runs [param sql], which may contain several statements separated by [code];[/code]. Result rows are discarded; use [method query] to read them. [param params] is an [Array] (positional placeholders) or a [Dictionary] (named placeholders) and is bound to every statement that has placeholders; their number must match. Returns [constant OK] on success, [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] if the database is not open, [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] for missing or unsupported parameters, [constant ERR_FILE_NO_PERMISSION] when writing to a read-only database, and [constant ERR_QUERY_FAILED] for other SQL errors (see [method get_last_error_message]).

method.name: get_changes
method.description: Returns the number of rows inserted, changed or deleted by the last [code]INSERT[/code], [code]UPDATE[/code] or [code]DELETE[/code] statement.

method.name: get_column_count
method.description: Returns the number of columns of [param table], or [code]-1[/code] if there is no such table.

method.name: get_column_names
method.description: Returns the names of the columns of [param table] in table order. Empty if there is no such table.

method.name: get_columns
method.description: Returns the columns of [param table] in table order, with their declared type, affinity, [code]NOT NULL[/code] constraint, default value and position in the primary key. Empty if there is no such table. [codeblock] for column in db.get_columns("items"): print(column.name, " ", column.declared_type, " key: ", column.primary_key_index) [/codeblock]

method.name: get_database_path
method.description: Returns the path the database was opened with, or an empty string if it is not open. Unlike [member Resource.resource_path], which is the file the resource was loaded from, this is also set for a database created with [code]SQLiteDatabase.new()[/code].

method.name: get_last_error
method.description: Returns the result of the last operation on this database or on one of its statements, [constant OK] if it succeeded.

method.name: get_last_error_message
method.description: Returns the message of the last failed operation, for example [code]near "SELEC": syntax error[/code]. Empty if the last operation succeeded.

method.name: get_last_insert_rowid
method.description: Returns the [code]rowid[/code] of the last row inserted through this connection, or [code]0[/code] if no row was inserted. For a table with an [code]INTEGER PRIMARY KEY[/code] column, this is the value of that column.

method.name: get_open_mode
method.description: Returns the mode the database was opened with.

method.name: get_row_count
method.description: Returns the number of rows in [param table] ([code]SELECT COUNT(*)[/code]), or [code]-1[/code] if there is no such table. [b]Note:[/b] SQLite reads the whole table to count its rows, which takes a while for big tables.

method.name: get_table_names
method.description: Returns the names of the tables in the database, sorted by name. Virtual tables (such as FTS5 tables) are included; views, SQLite's internal [code]sqlite_*[/code] tables and the shadow tables of virtual tables are not.

method.name: has_table
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the database has a table named [param table], ignoring case like SQLite does. Only tables listed by [method get_table_names] count.

method.name: is_in_transaction
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a transaction started with [method begin_transaction] (or [code]BEGIN[/code]) is active.

method.name: is_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the database is open.

method.name: open
method.description: Opens the database at [param path], closing a database that is already open. [param path] can be any path [FileAccess] can open, such as [code]user://save.db[/code] or [code]res://data/items.db[/code]. If [param path] is empty, opens the file this resource was loaded from (see [member Resource.resource_path]). A loaded file in [code]res://[/code] then always opens with [constant OPEN_MODE_READ_ONLY]. Returns [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if the database was not loaded from a file. Returns [constant ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND] if the file does not exist and [param mode] is not [constant OPEN_MODE_CREATE], [constant ERR_FILE_NO_PERMISSION] for a writable mode on a [code]res://[/code] path, [constant ERR_FILE_CORRUPT] if the file is not an SQLite database, and [constant ERR_FILE_CANT_OPEN] if the file can't be opened.

method.name: prepare
method.description: Compiles the first statement of [param sql] into an [SQLiteStatement] that can be bound and run many times. Returns [code]null[/code] on failure; see [method get_last_error] and [method get_last_error_message].

method.name: query
method.description: Runs [param sql] like [method execute] and returns its result rows. Each row is a [Dictionary] that maps column names to values. If [param sql] contains several statements, the rows of all of them are returned. Returns an empty array on failure; check [method get_last_error] to tell a failure from an empty result.

method.name: rollback
method.description: Discards the changes of the current transaction ([code]ROLLBACK[/code]). Returns [constant ERR_QUERY_FAILED] if no transaction is active.

constants.constant: Opens an existing database for reading. Required for databases in [code]res://[/code].
Opens an existing database for reading and writing.
Opens a database for reading and writing and creates the file if it does not exist.
